counties.notes:
King County, Washington (Seattle metro, pop. 2.3M, county seat Seattle) is the most populous Washington county, containing Seattle, Bellevue, Redmond, Renton, and Kent. The KingCo_Parcels MapServer layer publishes parcel polygons with three identifier fields: PIN (10-digit Parcel Identification Number), MAJOR (first 6 digits of PIN, identifying the parcel block), and MINOR (last 4 digits, the parcel within the block). No owner name, situs address, or assessment values are on this public REST layer. Washington State law broadly restricts owner-name exposure on public REST endpoints; King County follows this consistently. Confirmed live 2026-06-06 -- 638,577 parcels, PIN-searchable. For ownership lookups, use the King County Assessor's eReal Property portal at info.kingcounty.gov/assessor/emap/ (search by address, PIN, or complex name). The interactive Parcel Viewer is at gismaps.kingcounty.gov/parcelviewer2/. Bulk GIS downloads: kingcounty.gov/services/gis/GISData.aspx.

King County's open-data portal at data.kingcounty.gov runs on Socrata and does not carry a live, address-searchable parcel master table. The id tise-fzs9 surfaces in King County parcel searches; it identifies a Metro vanpool-ridership dataset, not parcels. Two Socrata tables carry the same PIN format used above and stay current: Property Legal Descriptions (id 4854-i48r, filter by parcel_number, https://data.kingcounty.gov/resource/4854-i48r.csv) and Real Property Tax Receivables (id dkna-i698, filter by account_number, https://data.kingcounty.gov/resource/dkna-i698.csv). Resolve an address to a PIN with eReal Property or Parcel Viewer above, then query either table with that PIN as the filter value. Parcel 0000200001, the same PIN in the ArcGIS sample query, returns its legal description at https://data.kingcounty.gov/resource/4854-i48r.csv?parcel_number=0000200001.

43 fields confirmed including PID_NUM, ACO_NUM, PIDMAP, parcel, exmp_code, exmp_amt, nbhd_code, nbhd_name, prop_use_code, prop_use_desc, tax_year, site_address, site_str_nbr, site_str_nbr_suf, site_str_dir, site_str_dir_suf, site_str_name, site_str_type, site_apartment, site_city, site_state, site_zip, soil_id, bldg_only_flag, vacant_land_flag, res_com_flag, appraiser_id, acreage, assessed_amt, taxable_amt, tax_code_area, inspection_cycle, parcel_location, land_value, asmt_year_exmp_code, asmt_year_exmp_amt, eff_from_date, eff_to_date, asmt_year, seg_status, Shape__Area, Shape__Length. NOTE: Owner name is NOT on this public FeatureServer, per Washington State law (RCW 42.56.070(8)) owner name data is restricted. Hosted on ArcGIS Online (services1.arcgis.com/ozNll27nt9ZtPWOn). counties.notes: Thurston County (Olympia, Lacey, Tumwater; FIPS 53067) parcel data is published by the Thurston County GeoData Center. The atlas lists no endpoint for Thurston: the endpoint was retired on 2026-10-20 after the county's reply of 2026-10-19 set out its data terms as non-negotiable. Term 8 bars making the data available to third parties naming Thurston County as the source, and term 10 bars commercial owner mailing lists. The terms are published at https://www.thurstoncountywa.gov/map-viewer-disclaimer/disclaimer-data. Owner names were never on the county's public layer; the mailing address was. If you would like this service, contact the county at GeoData@thurstoncountywa.gov and ask it to allow it.

coverage.summary: Thurston County's data terms don't allow sites like ours to show its parcel data, so we don't index it. If you'd like this to change, ask the county at GeoData@thurstoncountywa.gov.

counties.notes: Island County, Washington (county seat Coupeville) serves its parcels from the Assessor's own ArcGIS Server, joined to the PACS assessor data and exported nightly per the service description. The owner field is called taxpayer, the parcel id ParcelNo (for example R03213-384-4950), the site address physical_addr with its city, state and ZIP parts, and the owner mailing address mailing_addr1 to mailing_addr3 with city, state and ZIP. ParcelNo and taxpayer values carry trailing spaces, so trim on display, and some parcels (vacant land) have a blank physical_addr. Named outFields are accepted. CORS reflects the request Origin and sends Access-Control-Allow-Credentials true, so it is not a wildcard. maxRecordCount is 60000. The layer's copyright text reads DO NOT USE AS LEGAL DOCUMENT and no license is stated. Two sibling services carry the same data and serve as fallbacks: SmartGov/Parcels MapServer and Auditor/BaseMap MapServer layer 0. The contact URL is the county map server root, which answered HTTP 200 on 2026-10-03; no separate Assessor contact page was retrieved. Verified live 2026-10-03: owner SMITH returned rows (first owner SMITH, COLIN, R13334-372-1430).

counties.notes: Clark County, Washington (Vancouver; FIPS 53011). The county's own ArcGIS Server publishes the layer behind its MapsOnline mailing-label tool as MapsOnline/MailingLabels FeatureServer layer 0 ('Owner Addresses', one polygon per taxlot): 196,284 rows on 2026-10-10, every one with an owner name. The owner is MailName (the taxpayer mailing name) with MailCareOf (a care-of line, on 3,652 rows); the owner mailing address is MailAddrs (street line, padded with trailing spaces) plus MailCityStateCountryZip (city, state, country and ZIP in one string); the situs is SitusAddrs (street only) with SitusCityStateZip beside it (both blank on 17,980 rows); the parcel id is Prop_id, the Assessor's numeric property id (an integer, so search it with = rather than LIKE). The layer has no sale or value fields. Currency: DateOfParcels ('Parcel Publish Date') is 2026-10-09 on every row, so the layer is republished whole from the Assessor's parcels; it is the freshness field this record relies on. CORS: no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header is sent, with or without an Origin header, so a browser on another site cannot read it and corsEnabled is false; query it from a server, the metered API or the MCP. maxRecordCount is 5,000 with pagination. SIBLING NOT USED: MapsOnline/PropertyFinder MapServer layer 1 ('Taxlots', 196,283 rows, same Prop_id) also carries the owner, but it has no date field, gives the mailing address only as MailAddrs1-3 street lines with no city, state or ZIP (line 1 is sometimes a care-of name), runs city and ZIP into its single situs string, and its own description says it 'is still under development and may change without notice'. The Assessor's Recent Sales layer (LandRecords MapServer 6) had sales through 2026-09-29 and a publish date of 2026-10-02 on 2026-10-10. WASHINGTON LAW: RCW 42.56.070(8) bars agencies from releasing lists of individuals for commercial purposes, and some Washington counties (Pierce, Spokane) withhold owner names from their public layers for that reason; Clark publishes them on this public layer. No license or terms text is published on the service. Verified 2026-10-10: a count, resultRecordCount=1, an owner LIKE query (1,447 rows for %SMITH%), a situs LIKE query on MAIN ST (363 rows) and a point query at the county's internal point (one parcel, with an owner).

Pierce County, Washington (FIPS 53053). The county's public parcel data has no taxpayer name field. The county's layer metadata says taxpayer names are removed from public requests and cites RCW 42.17.260(9); that is the county's reading, recorded here as its claim. Without an owner name the data cannot answer an owner lookup, so this atlas does not index Pierce County. Parcel and sales records are available through the Assessor-Treasurer's parcel search.

basis.note: Pierce County's public parcel data has no taxpayer name field. The county's layer metadata says taxpayer names are removed from public requests and cites RCW 42.17.260(9). This records the county's own claim; the statute itself was not reviewed here.

coverage.summary: Pierce County leaves taxpayer names out of its public parcel data, citing a state records law, so we don't index it. Search the Assessor-Treasurer's parcel search, or request it and we'll tell you if that changes.
